messages:
incident-bot: [SEV2] p99 latency breach detected for dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42. Alerting on-call. metric: p99 > 5s for 5m, queue_depth=1200, warmup_pending=320, streaming_stalls=45. Incident ID: INC-2026-1765439999

alice (oncall): acked. I'm on it — grabbing logs + topology. Can someone confirm customer-facing impact? :eyes:

samir (support): Canary health checks show increased 5xx for a subset of customer routes. Early estimate: ~8% error rate for dedicated-backed routes, mostly streaming sessions. Customers with reserved pools flagged.

nina (sre): pulling metrics now. p95 rose from ~120ms -> 1.8s, p99 ~6.4s. Queue depth is spiking on the dispatcher for pool-42 shards 3/6. Warmup tasks backlog is high, warmup success rate dropped to 22%.

kai (eng-runtime): Recent autoscaler rollout (yesterday) changed handshake timeout from 15s -> 5s. If handshake is failing, instances won't join fast and warmup won't finish. Could be related.

alice (oncall): good catch, @kai. miguel, can infra temporarily increase pool capacity or extend handshake timeout? Need manual mitigation.

miguel (infra): I can bump target size for eu-west-1-dedicated-42 from 24 -> 40 and set handshake timeout back to 20s. Doing manual scale now. ETA ~4m.

ops-bot: Scaling request accepted: scale_pool pool=eu-west-1-dedicated-42 target=40 initiated by miguel at 2026-03-14T14:16:40Z

alice (oncall): while that scales, let's route high-priority customers to hosted fallback to avoid blocking. Which route key do we use?

kai (eng-runtime): use route override key `fallback-hosted-low-latency`. Will route to `redwood-open-3b-fallback`. I can flip policy for committed-customer routes. Doing a canary for 5% of traffic first.

nina (sre): evidence: logs show warmup tasks failing with TLS handshake timeouts: `Error: handshake timeout after 5s` across new instances. That aligns with the autoscaler change.

alice (oncall): @kai please widen handshake timeout to 20s for pool-42 immediately in runtime config and restart the scaler agent. Post the command you run.

kai (eng-runtime): running:

```
# temporary patch
curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/pools/eu-west-1-dedicated-42/patch" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \ 
  -d '{"handshake_timeout_s":20, "warmup_grace_s":60}'
```

ops-bot: PATCH accepted, config applied. scaler-agent restart queued.

miguel (infra): new instances are starting and registering. Warmup backlog decreasing: 320 -> 180 in last 3m. Queue depth 1200 -> 720.

samir (support): customer-impact update: two enterprise customers hit degraded streaming (higher stall rate). CS notified and we opened a priority ticket.

alice (oncall): continuing to monitor p95/p99. What's p99 now?

nina (sre): p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.9s across the pool (aggregate). Streaming stalls dropped to 12 in last 5m. Improvement correlates with scaled nodes and handshake change.

kai (eng-runtime): canary routing to hosted fallback running at 5%. No regressions reported so far. Increasing to 20% for affected routes to take load off dedicated pool.

alice (oncall): do it. Keep a log of time windows so we can roll back. Also, set autoscaler to prefer warm instances (hotshot) to avoid cold warmups during bursts.

miguel (infra): adjusted autoscaler policy: `preferred_hot_instances=true`, `burst_capacity_buffer=6`. Applying now.

ops-bot: Policy update applied to pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 by miguel at 2026-03-14T14:34:01Z

nina (sre): Retrospective metric: before fix, warmup success rate 22% -> after fixes 78% over last 10m. p99 trending down to ~800ms. Queue depth stable ~150.

samir (support): CS updated customers; one requested ETA for full recovery. We promised follow-up in 1 hour and offered to route them to hosted until dedicated pool fully healthy.

alice (oncall): good. Next steps: 1) keep on-call watch for 30m 2) run root-cause runbook and link to PR for autoscaler rollback 3) produce customer impact summary. Assign owners: @nina metrics, @kai config+PR, @miguel infra policy.

nina (sre): I'll capture graphs (p95/p99, queue depth, warmup backlog, streaming stalls) and paste to the incident doc.

kai (eng-runtime): I'll open PR to revert the handshake timeout change with explanation and add integration test for handshake under slow networks. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/autoscaler/pulls/1789 (DRAFT).

miguel (infra): I'll run a scheduled job to reconcile pool sizes across regions to avoid under-provisioning during daytime bursts. Creating infra ticket INFRA-7851.

alice (oncall): customer impact summary draft: ~8% of dedicated requests had elevated error/latency during 14:10-14:30 UTC, primarily streaming sessions; two enterprise customers reported degraded sessions; we mitigated by manual scale + handshake config + partial routing to hosted fallback. Continuing monitoring.

samir (support): noting that billing/usage spikes may occur due to routing to hosted for some committed customers — flagging finance.

ops-bot: autopager: paging resumed to infra on-call for 30m watch window.

alice (oncall): closing the active escalation. We'll keep the thread open for postmortem notes and timeline. Thanks all. :heart:

nina (sre): final metrics snapshot at 14:56 UTC: p95=160ms, p99=420ms, queue_depth=18, streaming_stalls=1. Mark as mitigated, will add to postmortem timeline.

kai (eng-runtime): PR opened and referencing incident. Will roll out autoscaler test tomorrow.

miguel (infra): pool size stabilized at 40, then scaled down to 30 after traffic normalized.

samir (support): CS follow-ups scheduled. No active customer escalations at this time.

alice (oncall): incident marked mitigated. Postmortem owners: nina (write), kai (fix), miguel (infra action items). We'll sync in the postmortem doc by EOD.
